status.en: 205 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 17% fewer than the week before, most of them in Abuja, Lagos and Kaduna.
status.nb: 205 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 17 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Kaduna.

summary.en: Gunmen continue to carry out attacks across northern Nigeria, killing civilians and security forces in Plateau, Zamfara and Kaduna, while bandits ambushed a police convoy in Zamfara and abducted six mourners transporting a corpse on the Benue highway. Troops rescued five victims of a Plateau village attack and arrested two herders searching for stolen weapons, but a mining pit collapse in Plateau killed one person. A building collapse in Nigeria has been reported to have caused losses of ₦4.6 trillion over four years and 321 deaths in ten years. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Våpenbærende menn fortsetter å utføre angrep i Nord-Nigeria, og dreper sivile og sikkerhetsstyrker i Plateau, Zamfara og Kaduna, mens banditter la en politikonvoi i Zamfara i bakhold og bortførte seks sørgende som fraktet en lik på Benue-veien. Tropper reddet fem ofre etter et angrep på en landsby i Plateau og arresterte to gjeterne som lette etter stjålne våpen, men et gruvedyp sammenraste i Plateau og drepte én person. Et bygningskollaps i Nigeria er rapportert å ha forårsaket tap på ₦4.6 trillion over fire år og 321 dødsfall på ti år. Konflikten førte til 1,486 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
